chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Sufyān ibn al-Simṭ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
When the sun declines, then the time of the two salats (prayers) has entered.

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, whose decline marks the prayer time
key_terms.الصَّلَاتَيْنِ: the two salats (prayers), meaning ẓuhr and ʿaṣr
key_terms.زَالَتِ: declined from the zenith; passed midday

ai.seo_question: When does the time of the two daytime salats (prayers) begin according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that when the sun passes its zenith, the time for the two daytime salats (prayers) begins. It is a jurisprudential narration concerning salat (prayer) times and indicates the legal entry of the shared period for ẓuhr and ʿaṣr.
